clue.text: Springs flowing back into drains

indicators.note: water flowing back runs the other way, so the word for springs is read backwards

parts.note: spas are mineral springs

explanation.surface: Spring water running back down into the drains.
explanation.definitionFit: Saps as a verb means drains or weakens, as in strength being sapped.

clue.text: Enterprise, say, puts sailors on board

indicators.note: to be on board is to be within the vessel, so the sailors go inside the word for board

parts.note: to board is to go on a ship, so board stands for ship here
tars is a common word for sailors

explanation.surface: A company, Enterprise, getting its crew of sailors aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enterprise' looks like a business but is the spacecraft from Star Trek; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The USS Enterprise in Star Trek is a fictional interstellar spacecraft, an example.

clue.text: Soften everything before I cut into spread

indicators.note: the paste is sliced open and the other pieces are placed within it

parts.note: pâté is a savoury spread

indicators.note: everything is placed ahead of I in the charade

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Instructions for softening a spread by cutting into it before spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: To palliate is to ease or mitigate, softening the severity of something.

clue.text: Craftily cad starts to lie over alibi. That's outrageous

indicators.note: done craftily means arranged with cunning, so these letters are reworked
the first letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A cad cunningly starts lying about his alibi, which is shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolical, literally devilish, is used informally for something shockingly bad or outrageous.

clue.text: Firm up belly suppressing every other urge

indicators.note: every other letter is held down and dropped, leaving the alternate letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Firming up the belly while resisting every other craving.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or urge someone forward to act.

clue.text: Stewed leg bones with a hint of oregano to make sauce

indicators.note: stewing mixes things up, so these letters are reworked
a hint is just a trace, the first letter of the herb

explanation.surface: A recipe: stew leg bones with a touch of oregano to make a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolognese is the Italian meat sauce associated with Bologna, served with pasta.

clue.text: Carobs have place on winding street

parts.note: locus is Latin for place, used in English for a location

indicators.note: a winding road twists, so the letters of the word street are rearranged

explanation.surface: Carob trees growing at a spot along a twisting street.
explanation.definitionFit: The carob is also called the locust tree, its pods once thought to be John the Baptist's locusts.

clue.text: Conservative party rises to expert

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the word for party goes backwards

parts.note: a revel is a lively party

explanation.surface: A Tory party climbing up to expert status.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever as an adjective means skilled or adept, close to expert.

clue.text: Promising fifty-one grand — see!

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
K stands for a thousand, a grand
Ely is a cathedral city whose bishop's diocese is a see

explanation.surface: An exclamation over a promising fifty-one thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not a command to look: a see is a bishop's diocese, here Ely, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something likely shows promise of turning out well, as in a likely candidate.

clue.text: Sailor left Spain for 7

parts.note: AB is an ... seaman
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A sailor leaving Spain for some destination numbered seven.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-reference points to the answer meaning clever; able means capable and competent.

clue.text: Subeditors should use this term with restraint

parts.note: a spell is a period or term of time
a check is a restraint or curb

explanation.surface: Advice that subeditors should use a particular term sparingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With restraint' reads as an adverb about using the term, but supplies a second word to join the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Subeditors correct copy, and a tool that flags misspellings is something they ought to run.

clue.text: 7 runner's squarely back to front

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow, like a sledge runner

indicators.note: the last letter is moved from the back of the word to its front

parts.note: full means directly or squarely, as in hit full in the face

explanation.surface: A runner squarely turned around, as in a race gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-reference points to clever; skilful means showing skill and expertise.

clue.text: Chaps welcoming tramp? Exactly so!

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the word for chaps holds the walking word inside

parts.note: fellers is an informal word for chaps or men
to tramp is to walk heavily

explanation.surface: Men taking in a tramp; the clue then confirms it is quite literally so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a vagrant but is a long walk; 'Exactly so!' signals that the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hikers on the fells, the hills of northern England, are people who enjoy a tramp across hills.

clue.text: Empty talk's thoroughly boring

parts.note: gas is idle chatter or empty talk
well means thoroughly, as in well mixed

explanation.surface: A complaint that empty chatter is utterly tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as dull, but is a noun: a hole bored into the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas well is a drilled shaft, a boring sunk to extract natural gas.

clue.text: 7 English soldier will shortly put back parting under canvas

indicators.note: the tent phrase is parted in two and the other letters placed in the gap

parts.note: camping means being in a tent, under canvas

indicators.note: putting back means reversing the order of the letters

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
will shortened to its contraction 'll

explanation.surface: An English soldier camping, leaving a separation for later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' reverses EGILL to LLIGE; 'parting' means the camping phrase is split to take it.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-reference points to clever; intelligent means mentally sharp.

clue.text: In general debts will amount to 7

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to pay debts

explanation.surface: A general observation that debts mount up.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-reference points to clever; ingenious means inventive and clever.

clue.text: Water spirit engulfs one in tank

parts.note: aqua is Latin for water

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so the spirit surrounds the letter for one

parts.note: rum is a spirit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A water spirit swallowing someone in a tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass tank of water for fish is the familiar home aquarium.

clue.text: Give authority to Democrat meeting European ambassador

parts.note: a legate is an envoy or ambassador, especially a papal one

explanation.surface: A Democrat meeting an EU ambassador to hand over power.
explanation.definitionFit: To delegate is to entrust authority or tasks to another person.

clue.text: Musically dramatic range — West mostly adapted that of the French

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so these letters are rearranged
most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: que is French for that

explanation.surface: A dramatic musical range from the West, partly adapted from French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of West to give WES; 'adapted' rearranges RANGE and WES into WAGNERES.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's operas are famously grand and dramatic, so music in his style is dramatic.

clue.text: 7 runs into wide bay

indicators.note: the runs letter goes into the word for the bay

parts.note: a bight is a broad curving bay
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone clever runs into a broad bay.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-reference points to clever; bright means quick-witted.

clue.text: Start going through revision in advance of A levels

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come ahead of A
a revised word has been reworked, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil starting revision ahead of A level exams.
explanation.walkthrough: A levels are the British school exams taken at about 18.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers, so they are levels of rock or society.

clue.text: Water drowning middle of littler ship's rigging

parts.note: rain is water from the sky

indicators.note: the central letters of the word littler are taken

explanation.surface: Water swamping a smaller boat's rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratlines or rattlins are the small rope rungs across a ship's shrouds, forming part of the rigging.

clue.text: Wearing suit rotter falls

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit
a cad is a rotter

explanation.surface: A rotter in a suit taking a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' suggests clothing but is a lawsuit, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, often a series of small falls.

clue.text: One's given command to stifle communist belief

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the officer surrounds the communist

parts.note: the CO, commanding officer, is the one given command
red is a common term for a communist

explanation.surface: An officer ordered to suppress a communist creed.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of belief, from Latin for I believe.

clue.text: Zola verged off course becoming glassy-eyed

indicators.note: going off course means straying, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The novelist Zola straying off course into a glazed stare.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes that have glazed over look blank and glassy, from boredom or tiredness.

clue.text: A taste for going round listed building site

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: a sip is a small taste of a drink

explanation.surface: A taste for touring sites of listed buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listed' is a pun: in Britain a listed building is protected, but here it also means leaning, as Pisa's tower does.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisa is home to the famous Leaning Tower, a building that lists.

clue.text: Representing first of rap artists on radio

indicators.note: read as re-presenting, the letters are presented again in a new order
only the opening letter of rap is used

explanation.surface: Rap artists being represented on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Transistor is a dated word for a small portable radio, named after its components.

clue.text: Novelist's change of direction eventually leading to love in Paris
